label: attack
description: A steganographic channel that encodes bits as zero-width characters placed only at word or punctuation boundaries, never between two letters and never as a run of three or more. The presence, absence, and identity of the characters carry the payload while the boundary placement keeps both the in-word and the run signal silent.

cases.title: Two-bit-per-gap channel encoding 'GO' between the words
cases.text: Please​‌ review​​ the​‌ attached‌‌ summary​‌ before​​ Friday‌‌ and‌‌ reply.
cases.rationale: Each word gap carries two zero-width characters (U+200B for 0, U+200C for 1), a run of exactly two, so the sixteen characters decode to the ASCII 'GO' with neither the between-letters nor the run-of-three signal firing.

cases.title: Base two payload 'OK' spread across the sentence boundaries
cases.text: The​‌ vendor​​ questionnaire‌‌ is‌‌ due​‌ back​​ by‌​ noon‌‌ tomorrow.
cases.rationale: Boundary-placed U+200B/U+200C pairs spell the two-byte message 'OK'; the characters sit against spaces, never directly between two Latin letters, and never accumulate past two, evading both zero-width signals.

cases.title: Two-character gaps carrying the instruction 'UP'
cases.text: Confirm​‌ the​‌ new​‌ endpoint​‌ is​‌ live​‌ in​​ the​​ staging cluster.
cases.rationale: A sixteen-bit payload ('UP') is distributed one bit per zero-width character in word gaps; because every character abuts a space on at least one side, zero-width-in-word and zero-width-run both stay silent.

cases.title: Inter-word bit stream encoding 'HI'
cases.text: Standup​‌ moves​​ to‌​ nine​​ thirty​‌ for​​ the‌​ rest​‌ of the quarter.
cases.rationale: The gaps between the words carry a hidden two-character stream reading 'HI'; the layout keeps each zero-width pair isolated from the next by a visible word.

cases.title: Zero-width pair channel hiding the token 'NO'
cases.text: Remind​‌ the​​ team‌‌ that‌​ the​‌ freeze​​ starts‌‌ on‌‌ Monday morning.
cases.rationale: The tag-channel here is the identity of a two-character zero-width pair in each boundary, encoding 'NO' while presenting to the detector as ordinary spaced words.

cases.title: Presence-versus-absence channel hiding a byte
cases.text: Schedule the​ retrospective for Thursday​ afternoon​ and​ book​ the room.
cases.rationale: This variant encodes one bit per gap by the mere presence (U+200B) or absence of a zero-width space, spelling the byte 0x4F; every occurrence is a single isolated character, so no run is ever formed.
